newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Lucent plans cellular plant in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Lucent plans cellular plant in Brazil.

text.p: Lucent Technologies Inc said Monday it plans to build a cellular equipment manufacturing plant and global provisioning center in Brazil, boosting its investment in the country to over $100 million.
Lucent said in a statement that construction of the factory, which will have a production capacity of 500 digital and analog cell sites per year, is slated to begin June 1.

Lucent said it plans to use the plant and center to develop software and systems for its Brazilian customers and eventually export to other members of the Mercosur trade bloc -- Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay and associate member Chile.
Production at the plant, to be built in Sao Paulo, would start late this year, it said.
The Sao Paulo facility, which would eventually employ 300 workers, would be Lucent's first in Brazil and sixth in Latin America and the Caribbean.
The plant also will house a technology and training, the statement said.

"The gigantic market potential was definitely a deciding factor in choosing Brazil as the location for this plant," Art Medeiros, president of Lucent Technologies Network Systems in the Caribbean and Latin America, was quoted as saying.

Brazil now has roughly two million cellular phone subscribers but the Communications Ministry expects that number to reach 15 million by 2000 as a result of privatization of the B Band cellular frequency and state-owned telecom firms.

"The unprecedented demand for mobile telephony services will require current providers to expand their networks and emerging wireless services providers, such as B Band consortia, to build entire new networks," Medeiros was quoted as saying.

The Virgilio Freire, president of Lucent Technologies Network Systems do Brasil, was quoted as saying that plant will help boost the company's participation in the market for cellular infrastructure equipment.
"Our goal is to reach wireless market leadership with a 30-percent market share and local manufacturing will help us get there," he said, according to the statement.
Earlier this year, Lucent signed $330 million in wireless infrastructure equipment contracts to expand the analog networks of state-run Telesp and Telepar.
Other clients include Telebras units Telemig, Embratel and Telebahia and CRT.

Lucent, whose research and development arm is Bell Laboratories, has 61 manufacturing plants in 22 countries around the world. Lucent was formed as a result of AT&T's breakup and became fully independent on Sept. 30, 1996.
